script: The US and Britain once knew their own wartime ally had massacred twenty two thousand prisoners, and stayed silent to keep him happy. By 1943, American and British intelligence had strong evidence that the Soviet Union, not Nazi Germany, was behind the Katyn Forest massacre. But the Soviet Union was a critical wartime ally against Hitler, and both governments quietly buried the evidence rather than confront Stalin publicly. American officers sent to investigate even privately concluded the Soviets were responsible, and their reports were suppressed for years. Polish exile groups who tried to expose the truth were dismissed as troublemakers threatening the alliance. It wasn't until decades later, long after the war and Stalin were gone, that declassified documents confirmed what Western intelligence had quietly known the entire time. The US and Britain once knew the truth about Katyn, and chose silence to protect a wartime alliance instead.

title: The US and Britain Knew, and Chose Silence Instead
description:
